Subject. GUERILLA AGENTS REQUEST PRINTING OF PROPAGANDA.
Made by. D.C.I. Wilkinson Forwarded by. P.I. Ducke

At 10.p.m. on the 10-1-40, persons named Zee Dah Tsang (徐大章) and Jung Ts Ching (倪子卿) shop assistants employed by one named Fong Ts Ching (方子卿) master of the Hsien Yue (祥裕) Clothing Shop, 176 Hokien Road, reported the following to this Station on behalf of their master.

At 4.p.m. on the 10-1-40, a male Chinese entered the above shop and upon ascertaining the identity of the premises, handed to Zee Dah Tsang a parcel and a letter and asked for help. The visitor then left the premises.

The letter upon being opened was found to state:-
"To the Hsien Yue Clothing Shop,

The Shanghai Branch Corp of the Eastern Moving Unit is hereby notified that we have at present decided to renew the propaganda work in the occupied areas, we have to ask the help of the public so as to carry on our work.

We learned that your shop is very enthusiastic in doing patriotic service of citizens, that is why we now request you to contribute material supply by printing 5,000 sheets of propaganda nature. Hoping that you will do this favor immediately.

A printing board is hereby forwarded.

Propaganda Section of
the Moving Unit.
9-1-40.

P.S. The following is a list of contributors, same could be referred to by telephone calls if you like to know:-

(1) Hwa Mei (華美) Dispensary - Contributed a printing sum of $30.00.
(2) Wu Ching Yue Daung (胡源興) - Contributed a printing sum of $60.00.
(3) Chung Ying (中英) Dispensary-Two rolls of white papers.

1940年1月10日晚上10时，受雇于福建路176号祥裕（Hsien Yue）服装店店主方子卿（Fong Ts Ching）的店员徐大章（Zee Dah Tsang）和倪子卿（Jung Ts Ching），代表其店主向本警署报告了以下情况。

1940年1月10日下午4时，一名华籍男子进入上述店铺，在确认地点身份后，交给徐大章一个包裹和一封信，并请求帮助。随后该访客离开店铺。

信件打开后发现内容如下：
“致祥裕服装店，

兹通知上海东部流动部队分部，我方目前已决定在占领区恢复宣传工作，我们需要公众的帮助以继续我们的工作。

获悉贵店热心于公民爱国服务，因此现请求贵店通过印刷5,000张宣传品来提供物资援助。望立即施以此援手。

现随函附上印版一块。

流动部队
宣传科。
1940年1月9日。

The parcel was found to contain a printing block, depicting Chinese troops fighting Japanese troops and was inscribed: "Contribute money or might. Try to enlarge our guerilla forces. Attack in order to put Japanese to death".

Also enclosed in the parcel are two ready made copies of the above print and two copies, each of other prints depicting similar scenes.

A description of the visitor was given as under:-
"Male Chinese, age about 23/4, height about 5'6", long face, pale complexion, long hair brushed backwards, wearing "Sun Yat Sen" style clothing and overcoat. Shanghai dialect",

but persons on the premises state that they have never previously seen this man, whose request, letter and delivery of the block, appears to be a demand for funds to aid the guerilla movement.

The copies of the block, also other prints are forwarded for information, and the block will be later taken to the Special Branch.

（批：In all probability a fix for the purpose of extortion or levying contributions. Det. and uniform men being trained to keep themselves at this shop. Wel）

Mr. Ding Kung,

Following the withdrawal of the national army, we,
guerilla units attached to the 9th Regiment, 16th Batalion of
the 108th Division, had been left in Shanghai. It is generally
known to the prominent merchants that we had inflicted appreciable
losses on the Japanese. The prominent merchants here have aided
us much by giving us cash derived by broadcasting through various
radio stations.

We have obtained the speech made by our leader
Generalissimo Chiang Kai Shek and this we have printed and distri-
buted to various people so as to make them understand that we are
frank and by so doing we can buy some more rifles.

The object of our writing you this letter is to
solicit you to contribute us with a sum of $658 which amount we
request you to wrap in a piece of Sun Pao newspaper and place it
in your alleyway near the mark          in white chalk at 8 p.m.
38/7/39.

Guerillas Units attached to 9th
Regiment, Western District.

P.S.

Regarding the banknotes, we prefer you to give us
in $10 denomination issued by the Central Bank of China. Please
treat the matter as confidential, as someone in Shanghai has
remarks "He does not know of our activities." If you disobey
our order, please take care of your hardware shop on Chungking
Road and your own life." "I have to thank you on behalf of those
refugees whom you are supporting."

(Sd.a Chopped) Yih Tseong Dah
An eleven year old boy scout.

Mr. Kuh S,
Our group have decided to send members to the New Area for
the purpose of making investigations regarding the movements of traitors.
As we are unable to collect any funds from this area, we request you
to loan us $200 or $300 for our daily expenses. We dont think you will
mind paying such a small sum of money as you are a well known patriot
and moreover your business is very good. We are in urgent need of
money therefore at 9 p.m. 29-6-39 deliver the money at Ningping Road
via the Garden Bridge, where one of our members will call for it. Do
not delay and keep the following five points in your mind.
(a) The delegate should wear white jacket and pants, no hat, and have
a Chinese white fan in his hand.
(b) Do not report to the Police or you could not buy your life even
with $300f.
(c) Only one man, not your employee, is allowed.
(d) An official receipt will be sent to you when the money is received.
(e) Keep the above four points in your mind and if you do not send the
money, you are a traitor and then your life will be in danger.

Chairman of the Traitors Special

Secretary.

you yesterday. As it is now the time for our monthly pay, we sincerely
hope that you will send the money. Our members are now in a critical
condition and we really can only offer courage, blood and life, but you
wealthy people should supply us with money in order that we can get
rid of the biggest traitor who is mentioned in the daily press. More
than 30 members are preparing for this chance, so please don't consider
that $200 or $300 is a large sum. The delegate you send should walk
on the left side pavement on Broadway Road at 9 p.m. 29-6-39 where one
of our men will receive the money, but if there is insufficient time
it can be delivered at the same time on the following day (30-6-39),

page_data.en:
Letter No. 1.

Mr. Ts Kwei,

Since the withdrawal of the Government Forces towards the west, a huge
group of guerrilla Corps have been stationed at Tsongming, Poh-sou and
Haimen with a view to continuing the mass resistance and annihilating the
traitors.

According to a report received from a member of the public, you have
worked in co-operation with the well known traitor Yue Choh Sung and
other for supporting the enemy with cotton which you have collected in the
area of Potung, Tsongming and Poh-sou. It is undoubtedly you have gained
a substantial profit by doing so. In view of the above, you will be
punished by the members of guerrillas in Shanghai according to the
national law, but I am in fear of a mistake in the facts reported, so I
have despatched more than ten intelligence officers to make thorough
enquiries over the past several months. I am now aware that you have
supplied cotton to the enemy who accept same for manufacturing gun powder
and/or the military uniforms, as the cotton is an important material,
especially during the time of war.

Your intention is to gain profit and you never think about the
unlawful deeds conducted, such as have been reported by the public.
Generally speaking, your conduct is injurious to the nation, and in some
way you will be executed.

I have long heard about your generosity, so I write you this letter
requesting you to contribute a sum of $200000.00 to be used by more than
10,000 members attached to this Corp. Please find a "Pass" enclosed in
the letter and deliver the demanded money by your representative within
10 days at a place, 3 li east from Kiang Ka Tsung village, Haimen, where
your representative will be met by our sentry. With the "Pass" you may
freely pass the sentry line and reach our headquarters. It will be too
late for you to repent if you fail to comply with our demand within the
limit.

(Sgd) Capt. Yue S Wei.
(Chopped) Yue S Wei.

Enc: It is hereby ordered that any sentry will give convenience to the
person in possession of this note for the purpose of approaching us
on important business.
(Sgd) Capt. Yue S Wei.
10-8-39.
This note is valid from the date of issuance to the 22-8-39.

第一封信。

徐子奎先生：

自从政府军向西撤退以来，大批游击队已驻扎在崇明、宝山和海门，旨在继续开展群众抵抗运动并消灭汉奸。

据一位市民报告，你与著名汉奸岳卓松等人合作，支持敌人，将你从浦东、崇明和宝山地区收集的棉花提供给敌方。毫无疑问，你从中获得了巨额利润。鉴于上述情况，上海的游击队员将根据国法对你进行惩罚，但我担心报告的事实有误，因此在过去几个月里派遣了十多名情报人员进行彻底调查。我现在得知，你已向敌人提供棉花，敌人接受这些棉花用于制造火药和/或军服，因为棉花是一种重要物资，尤其是在战时。

你的意图是牟利，你从未考虑过公众所报告的此类非法行为。一般而言，你的行为危害国家，在某种程度上你将被处决。

久闻你慷慨大方，故致信请你捐赠200,000.00美元，供本部队一万多名成员使用。信中附有一张“通行证”，请在10天内由你的代表将所需款项送至海门江家镇以东3里处，我们的哨兵将在那里与你的代表会面。凭此“通行证”，你可以自由通过哨兵防线并到达我们的总部。如果你未能在限期内满足我们的要求，后悔就来不及了。

（签名）岳S伟上尉。
（盖章）岳S伟。

附件：兹命令任何哨兵为持此条者提供便利，以便其因重要公务前来谒见我们。
（签名）岳S伟上尉。

Letter No. 2.

Mr. Ts Kwei,

On the 10-8-39 I sent you a letter in response to which you
inserted an advertisement in the local newspaper explaining your
position. However, I am not satisfied with your denial as to your
connection with "Yue", who being a "traitor" was "punished" by a
member of the "Special Mission" despatched by us. Since that time
he dared not be publicly active. A feast being prepared by him at his
home, you were, it was ascertained, also present as a guest. It is,
therefore, ridiculous to believe your denial. You monopolize the
cotton transactions, therefore if you do not sell the cotton to the
"Enemy", with whom do you make business transactions ? I never punish
any innocent people and as the facts prove you guilty your denial will
not be accepted. As to the method of "Redeeming guilt" it is good to
both you and us. Therefore, send us the amount demanded within the
period of time granted to you, otherwise rough action will be enforced.

(Chopped) & (Sgd) Captain Yue S Wei.

徐子奎先生：

1939年8月10日我致信于你，作为回应，你在当地报纸上刊登广告解释你的立场。然而，我不满意你否认与“岳”的关系，“岳”是一名“汉奸”，已被我们派出的“特别任务组”成员“惩处”。自那以后，他不敢公开活动。经查实，他在家里准备宴席时，你也作为客人出席。因此，相信你的否认是荒谬的。你垄断了棉花交易，因此如果你不把棉花卖给“敌人”，你和谁做生意呢？我从不惩罚无辜之人，既然事实证明你有罪，你的否认将不被接受。至于“赎罪”的方法，对你我双方都有利。因此，请在给予你的期限内发送所需金额，否则将采取强硬行动。

page_data.en:
Letter No. 5.

Mr. Ching Ts,

Since the withdrawal of the Chinese troops towards the West,
all Chinese citizens are filled with zealous desires in struggling
for the Nation, but why has your father committed mean deeds by
becoming a traitor for the sole purpose of making money. As you
are a well educated young man you should be acquainted with the
tendency of the national existence. However, what you have done is
just the same as what your unscrupulous and aged father has performed
Following a series of warnings delivered by this Corp, no reply
has been received. We expect you to advise your father to have
the money delivered in a few days, otherwise execution order will
be issued to guerrillas without delay.

It seems very funny that you think you are quite safe by
hiding yourselves from place to place and changing your car licence
plates, but I frankly tell you that we know your movements whenever
and wherever you go. In fact, if you dream to escape our law, you
are just playing with your lives.

(Sgd) Yue & Wei.

3-9-39.

On the envelope:-

Mr. Sung Ching Ts,
Yong Kyi Tuh Cotton Hong, 7/412 Kiangse Road,
Shanghai.

From Wei,
3-9-39.

第五封信。

程静慈先生：

自从中国军队向西撤退以来，所有中国公民都充满了为国家奋斗的热情，但为什么你的父亲为了 solely 赚钱的目的而做出卑鄙的行为，沦为汉奸。作为一个受过良好教育的年轻人，你应该了解国家生存的趋势。然而，你所做的与你那无耻年迈的父亲所做的完全一样。在本部队发出的一系列警告之后，未收到任何回复。我们期望你劝说你父亲在几天内交付钱款，否则将立即向游击队发布处决令。

你认为通过四处躲藏和更换汽车牌照就可以确保安全，这似乎很可笑，但我坦率地告诉你，无论何时何地，我们都知道你的行踪。事实上，如果你梦想逃避我们的法律，你只是在拿生命开玩笑。

（签名）岳 & 伟。

At 10.40a.m. 2-9-39 Sung Ming Ts, reported that
his father, Sung Ts Kwoi (孫子奎 ) had received a
threatening letter from a Capt. of guerrilla Corps.
Enquiries by D.S.I. Yang Peh Sheng, C.D.C. 157
and the undersigned ascertained the following facts:-
The informant and his father are co-partners in
the Young Chi Huh Cotton Hong, No. 7 Lane 412,
Kiangsu Road. On 10-8-39 the father received a
letter signed by Capt. Yue & Wei of 3rd route
Guerrilla Corps, threatening him with the death of
himself and his two sons if he does not send
$200,000.00 to the Corps at Haimen, and a pass was
enclosed to enable the messenger to reach Capt. Yue.
On 16-8-39 he received a reminder. On 23-8-39 he
received a letter and a magazine at the above address,
and a magazine at his home, 270 Rue Herniquin, F.C.
which he has since left and he refuses to disclose
his present address.
All three contained renewed threats whilst each
magazine in addition to a note also had one round of
Mauser ammunition enclosed therein. The letter
changed the rendezvous for delivery of the money
from Haimen to Quinsan. On 1-9-39 complainant
received a final warning stating that as he had not
complied with the demand steps would be taken against
him, unless he at once proceeded to Quinsan with the
pass previously sent.
The writer of the letter has apparently intimate
knowledge of complainant's movements and for this
reason the family has split up and refuses to divulge

Translation

Mr. To Kwei,

According to the report made by Wong Soong Kwei, the Capt.
of the 1st Group, you have failed to comply with the demand by sending
the money. It has also been learnt from the member of the Special
Service Mission of the Guerilla Corps stationed at Shanghai that you
and your sons are hiding at certain secret places, so as to make
yourselves safe. Regardless the law, you have changed your car licence
plates for several times.

You are excused due to your old age, therefore a series of warnings
have been repeatedly sent by us in the hope that you may change your
attitude. However, we are now well acquainted that you are willing
to be a "traitor" by supporting the enemy.

We hereby send you the latest and last warning and hope you will
promptly deliver the demanded money to this Corps, with the "Pass"
enclosed in the 2nd letter previously sent by us. Failing to comply
with our demand, you and other members of your family will not have
the slightest chance of escape or any form of remission; even if you
conceal yourselves in the Hongkow area or at Tokyo in Japan. Anyway
you will all be put to death, for it is too evident that you have
committed evil deeds. We hope that you will think deeply over this
matter.

Signed & chopped:- The 3rd Gp.
1-9-39.

杜贵先生：

据第一组组长黄松桂（Wong Soong Kwei）的报告，你未按要求
汇款。另从驻上海的游击队特别服务团成员处获悉，你
和你的儿子们正藏匿于某些秘密地点，以求
自保。你不顾法纪，多次更换汽车牌照。

念你年事已高，故予宽宥，因此我们反复发出
一系列警告，希望你能改变态度。然而，我们现在已充分知悉，你愿意
通过支持敌人而充当“汉奸”。

现向你发出最新且最后的警告，望你迅速将所要求的款项交付本部队，并使用我们此前第二封信中随附的“通行证”。若不遵从
我方要求，你及你家其他成员将毫无逃脱机会或获得任何形式的宽恕；即便你们
藏身于虹口地区或日本东京。无论如何，你们都将被处决，因为你们的
恶行昭然若揭。希望你对此事深思熟虑。
